title: GPU oscillation runbook prototype: probe and mitigation notes
content:
Summary:

This is a prototype runbook for a class of incidents we are calling 'GPU oscillations' — short, repetitive loss-of-progress events on a subset of nodes that manifest as brief resets, large latency jitter, or repeated per-GPU driver reprobes without producing a full kernel panic. These often show up as 1-3 minute windows of severe request degradation every few hours. They are distinct from single catastrophic panics and from purely thermal failures.

Observed symptoms (examples from last-week incidents):
- Spikes in request tail latency to 5-10x baseline for 30-120s, recurring every 2-6 hours.
- Node-level logs show driver bind/unbind messages and NVSwitch flaps but no contiguous dmesg panic trace.
- Correctable ECC counters increment rapidly then drain after a reset cycle.
- Users seeing incomplete generations with truncated token streams during the spike window.
- nvidia-smi shows GPUs in 'Unknown' or 'Lost' state intermittently.

Quick triage checklist (1-2 min):
- Check cluster health dashboard for recent recurring latency spikes and correlate to node list.
- Run 'kubectl get pods -o wide' to identify affected nodes and pod restarts.
- SSH to one affected node (if allowed) and record 'dmesg | tail -n 200' and '/var/log/messages' timestamps around the spike.
- Run 'nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,COUNT' and 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5 -c 12' to gather ECC and utilization traces during the next spike.
- If NVSwitch present, collect 'nvlink status' and '/sys/class/nvlink/*/link_state' for each GPU.

Detailed sample timeline (one incident, anonymized):
- 2026-11-29T02:14:03Z: Alert: 99.9p latency > 2s on route inference/generate for cluster-c.
- 2026-11-29T02:14:11Z: k8s events show 5 pods on node-gpu-17 Entering crashloop backoff.
- 2026-11-29T02:14:30Z: dmesg excerpt: "NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: irq 54: GPU reset required" then repeated driver rebinds.
- 2026-11-29T02:15:00Z: ECC counters on gpu0 increased by 120 correctable errors in 30s; other GPUs on node similar pattern.
- 2026-11-29T02:16:40Z: NVSwitch reported a transient link error between GPU0 and GPU2; link_state toggled.
- 2026-11-29T02:20:10Z: Node recovered, services ramped back, but 3 hours later pattern repeated.

Telemetry to capture (prioritize automated collection):
- Per-GPU ECC correctable/uncorrectable counters with 1s resolution for suspected window.
- nvidia-smi dmon series for utilization, memory, power, temp at 1-5s resolution.
- Kernel oops/dmesg windowed capture tied to pod request ids (correlate trace id).
- NVLink error counters and link_state snapshots.
- PCIe/BIOS firmware versions, driver version (nvidia driver build), and GPU microcode version.
- Host-level telemetry: pcie-aer counters, IOMMU errors, and AER resets count.

Reproduction probes (lab checklist) — run in isolated lab cluster:
- Recreate workload profile that generates long-lived KV cache streaming to saturate inter-GPU links while maintaining steady token throughput.
- Introduce targeted ECC stress using memtest-like pattern if supported by vendor tooling.
- Cycle NVSwitch firmware between known-good and bleeding-edge to observe change in flap rate.
- Toggle driver watchdog and enable verbose driver logging (NVreg_DummyPage) for a 24h sweep.
- Experiment with disabling ECC scrubbing via driver flags to observe effect on correctable accumulation.

Short-term mitigations (playbook actions to stop customer impact):
- Temporarily isolate afflicted nodes by cordoning and draining to move traffic off until next maintenance window.
- If the pattern is node-local and frequent, failover to Dedicated pool or lower-tier model variants until repro is resolved.
- For nodes with persistent NVLink flaps, schedule immediate firmware rollback to last known-good NVSwitch firmware during low traffic hours.
- If driver logs show repeated soft-resets without firmware change, increase driver reboot threshold in node supervisor to avoid noisy reboots (lower severity triggers only).

Operational runbook steps (safe minimal sequence):
1) Confirm repeated event (>=2 occurrences in 4h) for cluster/node.
2) Run quick diagnostic script: /usr/local/bin/gpu-osc-check which collects nvidia-smi, nvlink, pcie-aer, and recent dmesg to /tmp/osc-diagnostic-<node>-<ts>.tgz.
3) If ECC correctable rate > 50/s sustained, mark node for quarantine and escalate to hardware team.
4) If NVLink link_state toggles are frequent, capture nvlink logs and schedule firmware reflash to known-good with vendor ops involvement.
5) If no hardware evidence and driver stack shows repeated timeouts, roll driver to previous stable build on a canary node and monitor for 24-48 hours.

Longer-term engineering experiments and proposals: 
- Implement high-resolution ECC telemetry pipeline: stream per-GPU ECC deltas into time-series with anomaly alerts on burst patterns.
- Add link-state cross-correlation in observability: when NVLink flap occurs, automatically flag nodes within same fabric mesh.
- Create a software KV-cache backpressure control that reduces inter-GPU sharding to avoid saturating NVSwitch during transient error windows.
- Work with vendor to enable in-field microcode logging in non-blocking mode to capture firmware stack traces at the moment of link flaps.

Decision log (so far):
- 2026-12-02: Increased ECC sampling to 1s on cluster-c for a 72h window (owner: Priya).
- 2026-12-04: Disabled automatic device reboot on soft driver reset on experimental pool to reduce churn while capturing traces (owner: Amelia).

Open questions and unknowns:
- Are correctable ECC bursts a symptom or cause of NVLink flaps? Correlation found in 4 incidents but causality unclear.
- Do BIOS/PCIe microcode updates reduce oscillation frequency for a given node family? We have partial vendor data.
- Is there an application pattern that significantly elevates risk (large KV cache writes vs read-heavy workloads)? Need workload-level labels tied to traces.

Next experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Run targeted traffic that stresses inter-GPU communication on a canary rack with debug logging enabled; collect full firmware and PCIe AER traces. (owner: Diego)
- Implement automated capture hook in agent to attach request trace id to dmesg windows so we can match user-visible failure to kernel-level events. (owner: Jonah)
- Engage vendor support for controlled NVSwitch firmware A/B test with telemetry enabled. (owner: Priya)

Appendix: useful commands and scripts
- gpu-osc-check (prototype): collects minimal data
  mkdir -p /tmp/osc && nvidia-smi -q -a > /tmp/osc/nvidia-q.txt && nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5 -c 24 > /tmp/osc/dmon.log & pid=$! ; sleep 120 ; kill $pid ; tar czf /tmp/osc-diagnostic-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s).tgz /tmp/osc /var/log/dmesg* /sys/class/nvlink || true
- nvlink link dump: for p in /sys/class/nvlink/*/link_state; do echo $p; cat $p; done
- quick ECC counters: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | egrep -i 'Correctable|Uncorrectable' -A4

Owners and on-call notes:
- Primary on-call: eng-sre rotation (see pager duty) — escalate to hardware ops if quarantine threshold hit.
- Incident owner for current prototype: Amelia Chen (ameliac@redwood.ai).

Notes to self: this doc should be treated as a living prototype. Focus on automating the diagnostic gathering and ensuring we can reproduce the oscillation in a lab rack before pushing firmware changes widely. Avoid mass reboots of entire fleet; prefer targeted isolation and vendor-assisted firmware work.

End of runbook prototype.
